chief_complaint: decreased urine output and extreme weakness
hpi_details: 68M is brought in by his son. He has had a severe diarrheal illness for 4 days and hasn't been able to keep fluids down. For the last 24 hours, he has barely urinated. He is extremely weak and lightheaded.
concerns: son is worried about kidney failure

investigation_events.title: Urgent renal function assessment
investigation_events.availability_message: Urgent renal function results are now available. IV fluid resuscitation should not be delayed in this hypotensive, volume-depleted patient.

core_concepts: Caused by decreased renal perfusion (volume depletion).
common_misconceptions: Continuing BP meds (ACEi) in the setting of severe volume depletion, which worsens AKI.
dangerous_errors: Delaying fluid resuscitation, which can lead to Acute Tubular Necrosis (intrinsic renal failure).
management_principles: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, hold antihypertensives, monitor urine output.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 68M with severe diarrhea, poor oral intake, oliguria, and weakness.
reference_soap.objective: Dry mucous membranes, poor skin turgor. HR 110, BP 90/60. Labs show BUN 60, Cr 2.5 (baseline 1.0).
reference_soap.assessment: Pre-renal AKI secondary to severe dehydration.
reference_soap.plan: Hold Lisinopril and HCTZ. STAT 1L NS IV bolus. Monitor urine output. Recheck BMP.

learning_objectives: Recognize pre-renal AKI and the necessity of holding nephrotoxic/BP meds.

teaching.one_liner: Oliguria and elevated BUN/Cr ratio in a volume-depleted patient, exacerbated by ACE inhibitor use.

must_ask.say: Have you had vomiting, diarrhea, or reduced fluid intake recently?
Have you noticed a decrease in how much urine you're passing?
Are you taking any blood pressure medications, ACE inhibitors, or diuretics?
Do you feel dizzy or lightheaded when you stand up?
How is the weakness affecting your ability to do your usual activities?

history.answer: I haven't been able to pee almost at all since yesterday, and I feel so weak and dizzy that I can barely stand.
I noticed my urine dropping off yesterday morning, and over the last 24 hours I've only passed a tiny dribble once.
I had watery diarrhea about six to eight times a day starting four days ago, and I threw up whenever I tried to drink water.
I am terribly thirsty with a completely dry mouth, and whenever I try to sit up or stand, the room spins and I feel faint.
The single time I managed to pee yesterday, it was only a few drops of very dark brown, concentrated urine with no blood or foam.
No, I don't feel any blockage, burning, or straining, and my lower belly does not feel full or bloated at all.
No, I have never had kidney stones and I don't have any pain in my flanks or back.
No swelling in my legs or face at all, and I have actually lost about three kilograms since the diarrhea started.
I have had nausea and zero appetite, but no itching, hiccups, or confusion.
My heart feels like it is racing fast inside my chest, and my legs feel like lead weights whenever I try to take a step.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, skin rash, joint aches, or coughing up blood.
No, I haven't had a sore throat, runny nose, or skin sores recently.
No heavy lifting, no muscle soreness, and I haven't fallen or been stuck on the floor.
No, I haven't had any CT scans, dye injections, angiograms, or surgeries.
I took my regular blood pressure pills every morning like usual, but I haven't taken any pain relievers, antibiotics, or herbal tonics.
No history of heart failure, liver cirrhosis, or known kidney trouble before this.
A doctor told me my prostate was slightly enlarged a few years ago, but it has never caused any trouble or blocked my urine.
I'm so exhausted that my son had to help me get out of bed and walk to the car today.
I think I just got completely dried out from having diarrhea for four straight days.
My son got terrified that my kidneys are shutting down permanently because I stopped peeing.
I really hope you can give me some IV fluids to rehydrate me so I can get my strength back.
I have had high blood pressure for about eight years, but nothing else.
I had an appendectomy when I was twenty, but no other surgeries or hospital stays since.
I take lisinopril 20 mg and hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily every morning for my blood pressure.
No, I don't have any known allergies to medicines or foods.
I smoked half a pack a day in my twenties and thirties, but I quit completely over twenty-five years ago.
I might have a single beer on holidays, but I haven't had a drink in months.
I am a retired accountant and I live alone since my wife passed away.
Both of my parents had high blood pressure, but neither had kidney disease or needed dialysis.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, body temperature 36.8°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Marked drop in blood pressure with compensatory tachycardia and dizziness upon sitting up.
Dry cracked lips, parched oral mucosa, and dry furred tongue without pharyngeal injection or tonsillar exudate.
Flat jugular veins with undetectable jugular venous pressure even in the supine position.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally throughout all lung fields without rales, crackles, or wheezing.
Tachycardic regular rhythm without murmurs, gallops, rubs, or extra heart sounds.
Soft and non-distended abdomen; no tenderness, no suprapubic fullness, and no palpable bladder.
Mildly enlarged smooth symmetric prostate without nodules or tenderness; no rectal masses or gross blood.
Significantly decreased skin turgor with persistent skin tenting on the forearm; no skin rash.
No peripheral edema in bilateral lower extremities; capillary refill is prolonged at 3 seconds.
Alert and oriented to person, place, and time, though noticeably sluggish and fatigued.
